UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                               BEFORE THE
                 FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.                Docket No. ER27-25-000


                     MOTION TO INTERVENE OF ANNA FARRAR


 Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s Rules of Practice

 and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. § 385.214, I, Anna Farrar, respectfully move to intervene in this

 proceeding in my individual capacity.


 I am a resident of Warren County, Missouri, and a residential electricity customer of

 Ameren Missouri (Union Electric Company), a utility participating in the Midcontinent

 Independent System Operator (MISO) region. I have a consumer interest in the

 affordability and reliability of electric service and in the allocation of costs for transmission

 facilities associated with major new loads. My interest may be directly affected within the

 meaning of Rule 214(b)(2)(ii)(A), and my participation would also serve the public interest

 under Rule 214(b)(2)(iii).


 My interest is specific to infrastructure in my region. MISO has reviewed a proposed

 200-MW data-center load addition at the Rootbeer 345-kV substation in Warren County

 (EPR Project P50616) and a separate proposed 250-MW data-center load addition at the

 Montgomery 161-kV substation in Montgomery County (EPR Project P50086). Ameren

 Missouri has identified the existing Montgomery–Rootbeer 345-kV line in sworn

 testimony before the Missouri Public Service Commission (File No. EA-2026-0058).

 These records illustrate why I am concerned about cumulative large-load studies,

 network-upgrade attribution, and possible shifting of shared transmission costs to existing

 customers. I do not claim either project has applied through LARS or that any improper

 cost allocation has already occurred.


Docket No. ER27-25-000                                                                               1
  My preliminary position is that accelerated coordinated study of large loads and associated

 generation may provide efficiencies, but the proposed Large Load Addition Resource

 Study (LARS) tariff should maintain reliable cumulative analyses, transparent

 identification of project-attributable costs, and appropriate financial accountability.

 MISO’s filing raises questions about coordination between LARS, the Definitive Planning

 Phase (DPP) generator-interconnection studies, and subsequent MISO Transmission

 Expansion Plan (MTEP) projects. I seek to participate in the proceeding and address

 whether the proposed rules adequately protect existing transmission customers from costs

 they did not cause.


 I am requesting party status only on my own behalf, not on behalf of any organization or

 other person. I respectfully request that the Commission grant this motion to intervene in

 Docket No. ER27-25-000 and include me on the official service list at the contact

 information below.


 Respectfully submitted,

 /s/ Anna Farrar
